key_insight: In-place quantum multiplication and modular inversion achieve O(n^(1+ε)) gate counts for any ε > 0, with zero ancillas except for standard multiplication by a quantum multiplier.
engineering_relevance: These arithmetic primitives could reduce gate and workspace requirements in quantum applications while overwriting inputs directly with outputs.
method: Unify classical- and quantum-multiplier algorithms under one multiplication theorem.
Perform multiplication modulo 2^n with an odd multiplier and no ancillas.
Extend to standard multiplication with nonzero multipliers and to ancilla-free inversion modulo 2^n.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees and claims the first simultaneous subquadratic gate and sublinear ancilla bounds for these operations; it provides no empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on gate-count constants and hardware compilation overheads, which are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
